bug_semantics: An authenticated GET /download-export request supplied filename directly to download_export(), which concatenated export_path() with the raw $_GET['filename'] value and, after only file_exists(), passed the resulting path to response()->download(). A filename containing ../ could therefore escape the exports directory and disclose any file readable by the web-server account.
flaw_origin: Commit 0813dca72e26bca7f091bb7ffa2da3f3c18d7ac8 created FileDownloadController::download_export() with the unsafe raw-filename concatenation, added export_path(), and generated download links. Commit 5eda5fcf38a87a1ceb39762474df6c2211def9fb later exposed that already-flawed method as /download-export inside the auth middleware group; it enabled the attack path but did not originate the vulnerable pathname construction.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names author and committer danielrConfig <daniel@rconfig.com>; its message is only 'feat: add file download functionality and export path helper' and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, or bot trailer/identity.
evidence: The GitHub advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qrrp-6pvj-xfvf identifies authenticated traversal through the filename GET parameter in download_export(), versions before 8.2.13, PR https://github.com/rconfig/rconfig/pull/349, fix d133a466a2df9d065177de9a8ed50f1bfe438aee, and release https://github.com/rconfig/rconfig/releases/tag/core-8.2.13. In the validated full-history clone, `git log -L 21,38:app/Http/Controllers/FileDownloadController.php d133a466...^` traces the complete vulnerable method to 0813dca72e26bca7f091bb7ffa2da3f3c18d7ac8, where the file was added from /dev/null; `git log --all -S"export_path() . $_GET['filename']"` finds only that addition and d133a466's removal. `git diff-tree --name-status -r 0813dca...` shows a cohesive three-file feature commit: it added FileDownloadController.php and modified DeviceInventoryExporter.php and Helpers.php. `git cat-file -p 0813dca...` proves the sole immediate parent is 09fa5a4eac1abb8ee5010bb85b39411f36a6fa5e and supplies the human author/committer/message with no trailers. `git cat-file -e 09fa5a...:app/Http/Controllers/FileDownloadController.php` fails because the controller path is absent; parent-tree greps also find neither raw $_GET['filename'] nor function export_path. The added method contains `$path = export_path() . $_GET['filename'];`, `file_exists($path)`, and `response()->download($path)`. Commit 5eda5fcf38a87a1ceb39762474df6c2211def9fb adds Route::get('/download-export', ...@download_export) inside Route::group(['middleware' => 'auth']); both 0813dca and 5eda5fc are contained by core-8.0.0 and every later tag. `git grep` at core-8.2.12 still finds the raw concatenation at FileDownloadController.php:23. `git tag --contains d133a466...` begins at core-8.2.13, and `git grep` there finds the replacement containment check. The direct d133a466 diff reduces input with basename(), resolves the candidate and export directory with realpath(), requires a real file under the resolved export-directory prefix, and then downloads it. Although d133a466's commit object has a Claude co-author trailer, that is fix-only evidence and is excluded from BIC attribution.
reasoning: The lifecycle separates flawed-code authorship from later reachability. The BIC first created the restricted-base helper and the controller sink while trusting an attacker-controlled pathname; a later, small route commit placed that method behind authentication and made the flaw remotely reachable. The method survived unchanged into core-8.2.12. The referenced one-parent fix commit directly removes the unsafe data flow and is first present in core-8.2.13. The candidate is smaller and causally earlier than the develop integration merge 01545f2e39736641d170c13f2a71431c9fd4c6b5, the route activation, the release tag, and the fix, and it is not a move, refactor, revert, merge, or opaque squash. Direct inspection of its immediate parent tree proves the controller and exact sink did not exist. Finally, only the BIC commit object controls AI attribution: it has human author/committer identities and no AI marker, so the correct closed verdict is NOT_AI; the Claude trailer on the later fix cannot change that result.
